Skill School
Each Skill School will have at least 10 skills
Each Skill has 10 levels

You level up the skill by using it. Each skill will require Damage Caused, Health Recovered, Quantity of Times skill was used or any other that makes sense. The more the level go up the more difficult it gets to increase the level. Each skill will have its own evolution.
When you level up a skill the Skill School levels up. Also the skill itself gets stronger and may get additional effects.

Skill School level = sum of the levels of its skills, capped at 100 (10 skills x 10 levels). Maxing out 10 skills makes the skill school go to lvl 100 (max level). Schools with more than 10 skills reach 100 earlier, so players never need to max everything.
Each point in the Skill School improves its skills. Each point gives 1% power on that Skill School.
Power usually means increased damage or healing. But it can also increase status duration or effect (like +1 turn burn for power/20 rounded down, which means level 100 will give +5 burn turns).
The Skill School is a tree that spreads up into different branches. It starts with one or multiple basic skills.

To unlock new skills you need to meet some requirements of Skill School level and specific skills at specific levels. For example: to learn Ice Wall, the player needs lvl 20 in the Water Skill School, Ice Shard lvl 5, Rain lvl 3 and character lvl 15. This is the most basic way to acquire new skills.

There are skills that require conditions from two different schools. They unlock the same way: character level, Skill School level of each school and some skills at specific levels. They show up in both Skill School trees (for visualization). The level of a dual skill counts for BOTH schools. Most of these dual skills are related to the school adjacent to it, like Dagger + Dark may have a Shadow Step. There will be rare cases where skills from non adjacent schools have requirements. One example is a Shaman skill that may require Fire, Earth and Air / Electric.

Adjacency: the schools form a ring in this order: Bow, Air / Electric, Axe, Fire, Sword, Water, Staff, Mace, Light, Shield, Earth, Dagger, Dark, and back to Bow (Dark and Bow are adjacent). Adjacency only means a higher chance of dual skills. It is not mandatory that adjacent schools have dual skills, and non adjacent schools may still have them.

The most advanced skill requirement level is 80. You can basically learn all skills at Skill School level 80 (you still need to meet the requirements). I want to set that because even though the game can go to lvl 100, I want players to finish the campaign at lvl 80-82.

Some skill trees like Bow have only one start pointing that branch to many different skills. Others like Dark have many starts: Demonology (warlock), Necromancy (necromancer), and Dash (stealth, e.g. Dash > Shadow Step > Stealth). Dagger holds the dagger-related skills (e.g. Backstab, Throwing Dagger, Dual Wield Mastery) at later levels.

A skill that is a starter of more than one school (e.g. Slash in Axe, Sword and Dagger) is the same skill but lives in each tree separately and levels up separately (Axe Slash, Sword Slash, Dagger Slash).

Mastery skills are passive. Staff Mastery levels up by using any elemental skill. Weapon masteries (Sword, Axe, Mace, Dagger, Bow...) level up by causing damage with that weapon. Both mainly increase power, and can give other bonuses at high levels.
A skill only gains experience if the player adds it to the character's AI. Experience comes from using it. Values will be balanced later.
Weapon requirements are defined skill by skill, not per school. Example: an Earth skill that coats the dagger with poison requires a dagger.
A character can have only 6 to 8 skills equipped at the same time (exact number to be decided).

No skill is locked to a class, the class just provides the initial starting skills which will help you progress. Many skills are locked behind specific weapons to be cast. But nothing prevents a barbarian from learning demonology and summoning a fire imp. It will just require the member to learn the basic skill from a book and understand that gear may undermine certain skills if not on the 'correct' weapon.
